title: KP14 exposure on the profitability deviation with MIRRORED types b_f = [-0.15, -0.1, -0.05, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15] and a level ladder [0.5, 0.65, 0.85, 1.15, 1.5, 2.0]: the product of two mean-zero visible factors
question: With both factors of the product mean zero (type sign via size, profitability deviation via ROE), does KP14 get an interaction gap of 0.1/yr?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-31 02:00). vyge (hidden type) and vygel (type visible in size, R^2 0.91) both have room of 10-27%: with POSITIVE loadings the product b_f (eps - 1) is a monotone function of profitability whose slope varies by type, so a ROE sort takes most of it and the type only scales the slope. The campaign's rule (reduced form sign ladder, GS21's product): room needs the exposure orthogonal to every linear function of the characteristics, which a product has only when BOTH factors are mean zero. Here the loadings are mirrored (mean zero over types) and the profitability deviation is mean zero over firms; size reveals the sign of b_f through the level ladder, ROE reveals eps, and the premium b_f (eps - 1) is a product of two visible mean-zero factors, monotone in each given the other (no hump).

LOADINGS. +-0.45/0.25 (vygels, cancelled before running) and +-0.2 give NEGATIVE unit project values on the table grid for the negative-b types (y spends time far negative under Q, so e^{b y} is large there for b < 0: -8.5 / -1.6 / -0.3 at eps 0.1); +-0.15 keeps every type's unit value positive for eps >= 0.1. The effective exposure sd is about 0.24 b, so 0.012-0.036.

PREDICTION (2026-10-31): room well above vyg25's 24% (the pure product: 50% or more); fair gap +0.05 to +0.15. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 27% (vygel) on three seeds.
